evidence_summary.gap_reason: Standard sliding window segmentation. Could use a generic windowing atom but none exists yet. Low novelty -- standard signal processing primitive.
Novel temporal-to-SPD conversion using Hankel matrix from log-spaced delays. High-value atom unique to Barachant's seizure solution. No matching atom in any repo.
Transposed coherence matrix (freq-by-freq per channel instead of channel-by-channel per freq). Novel axis inversion capturing cross-frequency coupling. No matching atom.
Frechet mean on SPD manifold. Core Riemannian BCI primitive used in all 4 Barachant solutions. Available in pyRiemann (BSD) but not yet ingested as an atom.
SPD manifold to Euclidean tangent space projection with sqrt(2) off-diagonal scaling. Core Riemannian BCI primitive. Available in pyRiemann (BSD) but not yet ingested.

Segment-level max aggregation of sub-window predictions. Simple but domain-informed: mean AUC=0.674 vs max AUC=0.805. Could be a generic pooling atom but the domain insight (non-stationary seizure precursors) is key.
Rank-normalized prediction blending. Scale-invariant ensemble method using rankdata()/len(). Reusable across any multi-model ensemble. No matching atom.

architect_test_expectations.description: All 7 stages are gaps. The Riemannian atoms (mean, tangent space) are shared across all 4 Barachant solutions -- ingesting them would benefit multiple CDGs.
architect_test_expectations.critical_finding: This CDG has 4 parallel branches that merge at ranked_prediction_blend. The architect must recognize the parallel structure and not try to serialize the branches. The riemannian_mean_spd and tangent_space_projection stages appear on two of the four branches (autocorrelation and coherence).
architect_test_expectations.expected_retrieval_path: No atoms should be found. All stages should be reported as gaps. The windower stage is low-novelty and may be deprioritized for ingestion.
